items.titulo: Barça's €500,000 fine: Spain says a risk report is not a DPIA
items.resumen: Four high-risk criteria beyond Article 9, from 143,000 members to under-14s, sank the club's defence. What must a biometric login file show before it goes live?

items.titulo: Measuring Clicks Is Making ChatGPT Ads Look Like A Bad Bet
items.resumen: The first question marketers ask about every new advertising channel is almost always the same: Does it perform better than the last one we tested? It happened with social. It happened with retail media. And now it’s happening with OpenAI. The debate around ChatGPT advertising has quickly become a comparison with Google Search. Can it […] The post Measuring Clicks Is Making ChatGPT Ads Look Like A Bad Bet appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Microsoft rebuilds its bid model, citing 10% more value per click
items.resumen: Advertisers moving from eCPC to a CPA target averaged 18% more conversions, Microsoft says. Accounts with five conversions are told to skip eCPC from launch.

items.titulo: Microsoft Confirms Ads Are In AI Overviews On Bing Search
items.resumen: Microsoft has just confirmed that it is now shows ads in AI Overviews in Bing Search. We started seeing ads in Bing AI Overviews about three weeks ago, and Microsoft has now confirmed this on the Microsoft Advertising blog.

items.titulo: Build strategic A/B tests to grow your ad performance.
items.resumen: Improve your Google Ads performance with expert A/B testing strategies. Master AI Max experiments and Smart Bidding with our latest guide. Listen now.

items.titulo: Google AdSense Unifying Policies Into AdSense For Search Publishers Policy
items.resumen: Google announced it will update and merge the AdSense for Search (AFS) policies and Search ads policies into a single, unified policy set for AdSense for Search publishers. This will happen on January 17, 2027. Google posted a copy of the new, unified policy.

items.titulo: Only You Can Prevent JavaScript Security Hacks; AppLovin Eyes A Criteo Acquisition
items.resumen: What's behind the recent IT outages and cybersecurity scares? Plus: AppLovin is apparently among those in talks with Criteo. The post Only You Can Prevent JavaScript Security Hacks; AppLovin Eyes A Criteo Acquisition appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Safari's spatial CSS preview lets web pages place 3D models in a user's room
items.resumen: Six features sit behind a CSS Portals flag on visionOS 27.3 for web developers, while 3D models already render in Safari 27 elsewhere. Will ad creative follow?

items.titulo: Indie authors in 21 more markets can make five free AI audiobooks on Spotify
items.resumen: Spanish-language authors now qualify, and more than 60% of uploaded manuscripts get published, Spotify says. Can licensed voices close a 99 million-book gap?

items.titulo: AI chat trails search engines 17% to 39% in product research, DV finds
items.resumen: 55% of marketers measure the path to purchase with platform-native reports, ahead of mix modeling at 48%. Do holiday ad bursts suit the 74% who buy all year?

items.titulo: Only 6.9% of Americans' ChatGPT chats show intent to buy, SparkToro finds
items.resumen: Brand names appear in 12.1% of ChatGPT replies across 41,961 US conversations. Is ChatGPT a search engine at all, and how much room does that leave for its ads?

items.titulo: Don’t Give Privacy Regulators An Excuse To Come Knocking
items.resumen: Every time another state passes a privacy law or amends an existing one, brands have to tighten and update their vendor contracts. “If you’re doing business across state borders, your data goes everywhere,” said Patrick Turner, lead counsel for data and privacy at Ford Motor Company, speaking at an event hosted by the IAB in […] The post Don’t Give Privacy Regulators An Excuse To Come Knocking appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Google loses bid to overturn Colombia's under-18 data consent orders
items.resumen: Cookies on devices in Colombia count as local data collection, judges held, binding a US firm with no office there. What must Google now prove to regulators?

items.titulo: Google-commissioned test re-identifies 0.094% of targets in EU search data
items.resumen: Each match cost testers 3 hours, or €105, in data meant for rival search engines and AI chatbots. Will Brussels tighten its rules before sharing starts in 2027?

items.titulo: Character.ai's planned data sale gets a $650-an-hour privacy ombudsman
items.resumen: Lucy Thomson, ombudsman in 40 prior cases including Spirit Airlines, must report before the December 3 sale hearing. Do users' chats count as personal data?

items.titulo: Creators become a $116bn ad engine as Microsoft rebuilds its bidding models
items.resumen: Creator spending hit $116bn as brands hire creators to make ads, Microsoft rebuilt its automated bidding and France fined an insurer over plain-text passwords.

items.titulo: Ultra faces TINA.org complaints over 32m-view 'Zyn and Adderall' ad
items.resumen: Complaints sent Nov 17 to the FTC, FDA and New York officials cite 100+ health claims and marketing to minors. Will any of the agencies open an investigation?

items.titulo: 39 states and DC ask court to deny Disney's $20m Character.ai deal
items.resumen: Disney's hires get about $180m over three years, the estate $20m. Texas joins and says the order would bar regulators. Do users' chats sit inside the license?

items.titulo: Brainrot creators lose Genoa copyright bid over six ChatGPT prompts
items.resumen: Fifteen minutes of generic instructions failed Italy's amended Article 1 test for AI creators, who owe €8,059 in costs. What proof of authorship would count?

items.titulo: Elk River to pay $72,527 of $4.4m FTC judgment over Made in USA claims
items.resumen: Of 143 parts in its fall-protection harnesses, 68 came from abroad, the FTC alleges. Customers since 2021 get an email notice within 30 days of court approval.

items.titulo: Apple's California buyers face 2027 sales tax on dating, boosts and software
items.resumen: Developers lose proceeds to new 14% and 18% VAT in Botswana and Rwanda, and five storefronts reprice December 3. California's tax leaves their proceeds intact.

items.titulo: SiriusXM agrees to human-edited transcripts for 30 of its top-earning shows
items.resumen: Deaf listeners get speaker labels and sound cues on Pandora and Stitcher too, plus $1.465m in legal fees. Only new episodes count, and a judge must sign first.

items.titulo: Roblox's 14,000-word terms bind children to arbitration, Senate panel hears
items.resumen: Child exploitation reports from Roblox rose from 675 in 2019 to 65,381 in 2025 as hundreds of families sue. Can a sign-up tap keep their cases out of court?

items.titulo: Claude 4 absorbed Claude 3's hallucinations, 15-model ancestry map records
items.resumen: 10 of 11 open-weight models lean on closed AI, and 2,778 dependencies sit behind the 15 mapped. Should AI transparency rules reach further up the supply chain?

items.titulo: HubSpot won't charge extra when Claude or ChatGPT works its CRM
items.resumen: Outside agents on its APIs use plan limits of 250,000 to 1 million daily calls, not credits. What will agents in its governed environment cost, and from when?

items.titulo: 1,486 newsletters on Ghost charge exactly the platform's $5 default
items.resumen: Of 20,868 paid newsletters, 72% charge $5 to $8 a month and finance tops 29 topics at $29. How much do Substack and Ghost fees leave publishers of each payment?

items.titulo: WHOOP signs four-year Formula 1 deal to put drivers' body data on air
items.resumen: FIA clears the bicep-worn strap for racing from this weekend in Las Vegas, a first for a consumer wearable. Which readings go on air, and who controls them?

items.titulo: Spotify publishes 11 romance audiobooks from eight independent authors
items.resumen: Two of eight writers return from the 2025 debut cohort of 16, with stories of 10,000 to 40,000 words. What does a music app gain by becoming the publisher too?

items.titulo: Grindr's $120-a-month shortcut: five AI-picked profiles a day
items.resumen: Weekly billing at $70 comes to $303 a month for US users, and HIV status stays out of the AI. What does a capped premium tier mean for the free users ads reach?

items.titulo: Chinese studio Gryphline wins Google Play's Best Game outside Japan and Korea
items.resumen: Best Game in Japan and Korea went to hololive Dreams and MapleStory: Idle RPG; India and Indonesia rewarded local studios. What do 17 winners say about APAC?

items.titulo: Google's Gemini agent now shares a name with its 8-year-old to-do app
items.resumen: Gemini's free Tasks mode and the Google Tasks app both promise to handle to-dos, and Gemini already links to that app. Google has not said how the two coexist.

items.titulo: Apple waives its $14.99 Apple TV fee for F1's Las Vegas Grand Prix
items.resumen: Five sessions across three days, up to 30 extra feeds and Spanish commentary for US fans. Univision and Tubi carry the race. What does a free race buy Apple?

items.titulo: Keke Palmer's Wondery show wins Apple Podcasts' 2026 Show of the Year
items.resumen: Amazon-owned Wondery has produced two of the last three winners, and this one ranks among Apple's top video shows. What does the pick tell podcast advertisers?

items.titulo: Apple lets Mac users limit apps to chosen folders, not the whole disk
items.resumen: Mac AI agents and automation tools face a split Device Control setting in macOS 27.3 beta 2. Old grants stay in place, but how will new installs onboard users?

items.titulo: Chess, cats and a clipboard: Apple picks its 45 App Store Award finalists
items.resumen: Cultural Impact now splits into six apps and six games, and Google Play's Best Game, Arknights: Endfield, makes the iPad list. Winners are due within weeks.

items.titulo: Daily Search Forum Recap: November 19, 2026
items.resumen: Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today...

items.titulo: Google Hotel Search Listings With Continue On Google To Book
items.resumen: Google seems to be rolling out hotel booking directly on Google in Google Search but through AI Mode. So when you search on Google and Google shows you the hotels, you can now click on a button that says "Continue on Google" and it then takes you through the AI Mode hotel booking feature to book using your Google account.

items.titulo: Top pharma search result wins Google AI Overview citation 69% of the time
items.resumen: Drug brand sites held 9.2% of No. 1 rankings but drew 4.2% of citations across five therapy areas; Reddit got 0.15%. Can visibility stand in for lost traffic?

items.titulo: Google's AI cited Oasis LMS's own list, then recommended four rivals
items.resumen: Brands missed Google's AI pick in 224 of 323 citations of their own lists, Hordus AI says, citing June data. Why does Google cite the page but not the brand?

items.titulo: Instagram tests Direct, a chat app that needs no Instagram account
items.resumen: Türkiye and Thailand test the 13+ app first, with Instagram chats synced and strangers kept out. Meta has yet to say where ads and business messages fit in.

items.titulo: Meta's Muse reaches Australia with 9 local partners, from Canva to Kogan
items.resumen: Australian users get voice and spaces on day one, 12 days after voice began US-only. Property portals sign on too. When do the nine partner connectors go live?

items.titulo: Google Data Feed Validation Tool Has Been Turned Down
items.resumen: Google has "turned down" its Data Feed validation tool and has removed references to it from the Book actions (Book) structured data help documentation. I am not sure when this tool surfaced but likely sometime between October 2016 and December 2017 alongside the broader Actions on Google developer platform.

items.titulo: Google Images Results With Lens To AI Mode Feature
items.resumen: Google image search results now let you click a Google Lens button, which takes you into an AI Overview follow-up query or even an AI Mode follow-up query. This is different from when Google added the Google Lens button to image search results.

items.titulo: Google Search Tests "Show Original Results" Button
items.resumen: Google Search is testing a new button in the search results named "Show original results." It seems this button does something similar to the "Search instead for" link, where Google will auto correct or adapt your query when it thinks you have a typo in your query or you meant to search for something else.

items.titulo: Google Search What People Are Saying AI-Generated Emojis
items.resumen: Google seems to be placing emojis in the AI-generated "What people are saying" box in Google Search. Google does show emojis in its search results, but these emojis are not coming from the website it is referencing, but rather from Google Search and its AI-generated descriptions.

items.titulo: Google says DV360 vertical video cut Ford's cost per unique user 19%
items.resumen: Loblaw Advance shopper data with SKU-level sales tracking reaches DV360 buyers in Canada. What does Google leave out of the Ford test, and can anyone check it?

items.titulo: Sky Media shifts addressable TV ads to the homes that respond, mid-campaign
items.resumen: Data from 500-plus advertisers shapes the opening plan, then live household signals refine it. A beta runs now, full rollout in 2027, but which outcomes count?

items.titulo: InMobi lets seven AI agents run small firms' Google, Meta and ChatGPT ads
items.resumen: Just 4% of 800 US small advertisers and agencies can launch a campaign the same day, per InMobi's survey. Who checks the True ROAS figure the new tool reports?

items.titulo: Nexxen ads beat DISQO awareness benchmark by 305%, Nexxen says
items.resumen: Favorability ran 66% and purchase intent 40% above DISQO norms on US campaigns. Without a campaign count, how much weight can the 20-month comparison carry?

items.titulo: Meet OpenX’s New CEO, An Optimistic Realist
items.resumen: Safari is cracking down on identity vendors, DSPs are going direct to publishers, Google gets to keep AdX, agents are threatening to cut out the middlemen, the walled gardens keep winning and the open web is under pressure. Happy first week, Robert. In early November, OpenX named Robert Horler as its new CEO, taking the […] The post Meet OpenX’s New CEO, An Optimistic Realist appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Vistar adds two New Zealand hires as programmatic revenue nearly doubles
items.resumen: Agencies buying New Zealand screens: programmatic DOOH was US$15.2m in 2025, 86.4% via specialist DSPs. Vistar gives no base, so how large is nearly double?

items.titulo: Target's ad revenue climbs 23% to $296m in third quarter
items.resumen: Non-merchandise sales rose 19.3% and digital comps 9.8% for brands buying Roundel ads, but $301m of tariff refunds flatters profit. What lasts past December?

items.titulo: Loblaw lets Meta's Muse plan meals and check out groceries in Canada
items.resumen: Canadian shoppers get Muse's first local retail connector as Google adds Loblaw audiences to DV360 the same day. Which banners join, and where does the data go?

items.titulo: Amazon's ad agent can't see why three campaigns stopped serving
items.resumen: Zero impressions since Nov 15, yet the agent told the advertiser bids, budgets and status were out of reach. Amazon sells it on troubleshooting. Which is right?

items.titulo: Amazon's gambling ad rules get a new name, not a single new line
items.resumen: Real money gaming is now Gambling and games on Amazon's list for gambling advertisers. Rules for 22 countries keep their Nov 15 text; other labels stay put.

items.titulo: Amazon's free Brand Store quiz narrows up to 50 products with four questions
items.resumen: Brand owners in 25 marketplaces get up to six answers per question and a four-product fallback. Missing from the guide: any data on what shoppers answered.

items.titulo: Nearly 3 in 4 Walmart test-and-treat visits come after 5 p.m. or on weekends
items.resumen: Pharmacists at more than 1,500 Walmart pharmacies in 24 states can test and prescribe in one visit. How far the service reaches still depends on state laws.

items.titulo: CBP rule forces a third of foreign importers to change customs brokers
items.resumen: Only 663 broker filer codes can file entries for foreign importers without CTPAT status, Amazon sellers among them. Can that list absorb the switch in time?
